# Torque, power and bus-timing budget (generated by `python -m analysis.report`; do not edit)

Generated 2026-11-25. Inputs: spec/kinematics.yaml (masses, lengths, servo ratings incl. `servo_overrides`, payload 0.2 kg); centres of mass from the generated CAD (hardware/cad). Nothing has been measured on hardware.

## 1. Static holding torque, arm stretched horizontally, payload at the TCP

Servos: STS3215 stall 2.9 N*m, continuous = 40% of stall = 1.16 N*m. Shoulder (spec v1.3): STS3250-C001, stall 4.9 N*m, continuous 1.96 N*m on the same 40 % rule (the listed "rated" torque is 1.57 N*m, so treat the shoulder's continuous figures as optimistic by ~20 %). No counterbalance spring (section 2).

| joint | model | servo | holding N*m | % stall | margin vs continuous | verdict |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| shoulder_pitch | spec masses | STS3250-C001 | 2.35 | 48 % | x0.84 | intermittent only |
| elbow_pitch | spec masses | STS3215 | 1.15 | 40 % | x1.01 | OK continuous |
| wrist_pitch | spec masses | STS3215 | 0.30 | 11 % | x3.81 | OK continuous |
| shoulder_pitch | CAD masses | STS3250-C001 | 2.38 | 48 % | x0.83 | intermittent only |
| elbow_pitch | CAD masses | STS3215 | 1.22 | 42 % | x0.95 | intermittent only |
| wrist_pitch | CAD masses | STS3215 | 0.35 | 12 % | x3.27 | OK continuous |
| wrist_roll | CAD | STS3215 | 0.045 | 1.5 % | x26 | OK (payload on axis; gripper COM 23 mm off axis) |
| base_yaw | spec | STS3215 | 0 (vertical axis); dynamic: I_zz 0.099 kg*m^2 x 15 rad/s^2 = 1.49 | 51 % | x0.78 | peak only; limit yaw accel at full reach |
| gripper | - | STS3215 | squeeze force per jaw at stall 77 N, at continuous 31 N | needed for 0.2 kg (mu 0.5, SF 2.0): 3.9 N | x7.9 | OK; set a gripper current limit so it cannot crush objects |

Over the whole reachable pose set (shoulder in [-1.80, +0.60] rad, elbow and wrist over their full limits, payload 0 or the spec payload) the worst shoulder holding torque is **2.35 N*m** = 48 % of the STS3250-C001 stall torque.

Largest payload that the servos can hold CONTINUOUSLY (40 % derating) at full horizontal reach: elbow **0.20 kg**, shoulder **0.12 kg** (STS3250-C001). The spec's 0.2 kg at full reach is therefore an intermittent (seconds) load for shoulder and elbow; for long data sessions keep heavy objects inside ~80 % reach.

Bearing load (yaw): overturning moment at full reach with payload = 2.35 N*m (spec masses) plus the shoulder bracket; carried by the 61816 thin-section bearing (80 x 100 x 10), not by the yaw servo.

## 2. Why there is no counterbalance spring (spec v1.3)

A zero-free-length spring (cable from a pin 70 mm along the upper arm over a pulley 40 mm above the shoulder axis) sized minimax over the reachable poses needs K = k*a*b = 1.20 N*m: rate 0.43 N/mm, up to 42 N, 74 mm extension. The shortest music-wire extension spring for that (static shear <= 800 MPa: wire 1.4 mm, mean dia 18.2 mm) is **125 mm long at full extension**, against ~79 mm available on the shoulder bracket. Taller posts, a moved pin, 2:1 reeving, parallel springs and partial balance were all checked and none fits, because the spring has to store ~1.9 J. The spring, post, pulley and pin were therefore removed and the shoulder servo became an STS3250 (same case, 4.9 N*m stall): spec/DECISIONS.md, v1.3.

## 3. 12 V servo-rail current budget

Linear current model per servo: I = 0.05 A idle (assumed) + (I_stall - idle) x tau/tau_stall (STS3250 stall current 4.2 A from retailer listings; verify).

| joint | servo | static tau N*m | I (A) | stall I (A) |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| base_yaw | STS3215 | 0.00 | 0.05 | 2.7 |
| shoulder_pitch | STS3250-C001 | 2.38 | 2.06 | 4.2 |
| elbow_pitch | STS3215 | 1.22 | 1.16 | 2.7 |
| wrist_pitch | STS3215 | 0.35 | 0.37 | 2.7 |
| wrist_roll | STS3215 | 0.04 | 0.09 | 2.7 |
| gripper | STS3215 | 0.00 | 0.05 | 2.7 |
| **sum static** | | | **3.79** | **17.7** |

Board electronics (5 V + 3.3 V bucks, ~0.63 W at 85 %): 0.06 A at 12 V.

| case | 12 V current |
|---|---|
| static hold at full reach + payload | 3.9 A |
| typical worst motion: static + the two largest servos accelerating at 80 % stall | 9.4 A |
| absolute worst: all six servos stalled at once | 17.8 A |

**PSU recommendation:** 12 V, **>= 12.5 A continuous (150 W)**, with a peak rating >= 18 A for >= 100 ms or a hard current limit that does not latch off. Rationale: the realistic worst motion is ~9 A; an all-servo stall (18 A) exceeds a 12.5 A brick, so the firmware current limits must keep the sum below it. Firmware/servo settings: per-servo protection current ~2.0 A (~3.0 A for the STS3250 shoulder), board OVERCURRENT fault at 12 A sustained > 20 ms on the INA240 reading. Input fuse 15 A slow-blow. Bulk capacitance on the servo rail (>= 1000 uF low-ESR) covers sub-millisecond stall edges only, not sustained stalls.

## 4. Servo bus timing (spec/protocol.md: 1 kHz loop, 1 Mbps, SYNC_WRITE 6 + 1 read per cycle)

### goal position only (2 B/servo)

| item | us |
|---|---|
| SYNC_WRITE (26 B) | 260 |
| READ request (8 B) | 80 |
| turnaround tx->rx | 2 |
| servo latency (assumed) | 100 |
| status reply (21 B) | 210 |
| turnaround rx->tx | 2 |
| CPU/DMA slack (assumed) | 30 |
| **total** | **684** (68% of the 1000 us cycle, margin 316 us) |

### position + time + speed (6 B/servo)

| item | us |
|---|---|
| SYNC_WRITE (50 B) | 500 |
| READ request (8 B) | 80 |
| turnaround tx->rx | 2 |
| servo latency (assumed) | 100 |
| status reply (21 B) | 210 |
| turnaround rx->tx | 2 |
| CPU/DMA slack (assumed) | 30 |
| **total** | **924** (92% of the 1000 us cycle, margin 76 us) |

8N1 framing (10 bits/byte). The read covers registers 0x38-0x46 (present position, speed, load, voltage, temperature, status, moving, present current) in one READ so the STATE frame gets pos/vel/current/temp from one transaction. Feetech packet layout as in the SCS/STS protocol (Dynamixel-1.0-like); register addresses are from the STS3215 memory table as commonly published and must be checked against the servo's datasheet. Servo response latency is ASSUMED (100 us); measure it on the first servo with a logic analyser. Verdict: fits in 1 ms with the 2-byte write; the 6-byte write is tight but fits; there is no room for a second read per cycle.
